headline: A preprint reports measurable handshake overhead across three AI agent protocols
summary: An arXiv preprint reports a phase-decomposed benchmark of MCP, A2A and ACP agent-startup overhead using their official Python SDKs. For MCP revision 2026-07-28, the official specification removed the initialize/initialized exchange and protocol sessions; the paper uses “handshake” operationally for discovery through task readiness, including server/discover. In its stated setup, the authors report 50 runs per cell and, under a userspace-emulated 50 ms application-layer RTT, median cold-start times of 230 ms for legacy MCP, 122 ms for modern MCP, 61.0 ms for A2A and 62.1 ms for ACP. The paper also reports capability-metadata costs of 24–107 tokens per capability. These are author-reported benchmark results from minimal echo agents, not independent reproduction or measured production workloads. The paper's HTML says experiments ran on 10 Aug 2026, while the linked repository README says the paper's measurements were taken on 30 Sep; the arXiv v1 submission history says 12 Aug even though arXiv's cs.AI new-submission list showed the record on 23 Oct. This chronology and raw-artifact binding remain unresolved.
